'''LaplacesDemon''' is an [[open-source software|open-source]] [[statistical package]] that is intended to provide a complete environment for [[Bayesian inference]]. LaplacesDemon has been used in numerous fields.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Bolker BM, Gardner B, Maunder M, Berg CW, Brooks M, Comita L, Crone E, Cubaynes S, Davies T, de Valpine P, Ford J, Gimenez O, Kery M, Kim EJ, Lennert-Cody C, Magnusson A, Martell S, Nash J, Nielsen A, Regetz J, Skaug H, Zipkin E|title=Strategies for Fitting Nonlinear Ecological Models in R, AD Model Builder, and BUGS|journal=Methods in Ecology and Evolution|year=2013|volume=4|issue=6|pages=501–512|doi=10.1111/2041-210X.12044|doi-access=free|bibcode=2013MEcEv...4..501B }}<!--|accessdate=10 March 2014--></ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Gallo|first=E|author2=Miller B |author3=Fender R |title=Assessing luminosity correlations via cluster analysis: Evidence for dual tracks in the radio/X-ray domain of black hole X-ray binaries|journal=[[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]]|year=2012|volume=423|issue=1|pages=590–599|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2966.2012.20899.x|doi-access=free|arxiv=1203.4263|bibcode=2012MNRAS.423..590G}}<!--|accessdate=22 February 2014--></ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Maurya|first=M |author2=Vishwakarma, UK |author3=Lohia, P|title=A Study of Statistical Inference Tools for Uncertainty Reasoning in Target Tracking|journal=International Journal of Computer Networking, Wireless and Mobile Communications|year=2013|volume=3|issue=3|pages=1–10}}<!-- |accessdate=22 February 2014 --></ref> The user writes their own model specification function and selects a numerical approximation algorithm to update their Bayesian model. Some numerical approximation families of algorithms include [[Laplace's method]] (Laplace approximation), [[numerical integration]] (iterative quadrature), [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] (MCMC), and [[variational Bayesian methods]].

The base package, LaplacesDemon, is written entirely in the [[R programming language]], and is largely self-contained, though it does require the parallel package for high performance computing via parallelism. [[Big data]] is also supported.<ref>{{cite web|title=Big Data and Bayesian Inference|url=http://www.bayesian-inference.com/softwarearticlesbigdata|work=bayesian-inference.com|publisher=Statisticat, LLC.|accessdate=22 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226003504/http://www.bayesian-inference.com/softwarearticlesbigdata|archive-date=26 February 2014|url-status=usurped}}</ref> An extension package called LaplacesDemonCpp is in development to provide [[C++]] functionality.<ref>{{cite web|title=C++ is Sugar for LaplacesDemon|url=http://www.bayesian-inference.com/softwarearticlescppsugar|work=bayesian-inference.com|publisher=Statisticat, LLC.|accessdate=8 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512222343/http://www.bayesian-inference.com/softwarearticlescppsugar|archive-date=12 May 2014|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

The software was named after the concept of [[Laplace's demon]], which refers to a hypothetical being capable of predicting the universe. [[Pierre-Simon Laplace]] alluded to this hypothetical being in the introduction to his Philosophical Essay on Probabilities.<ref>Pierre-Simon Laplace, "[https://archive.org/details/philosophicaless00lapliala A Philosophical Essay on Probabilities]" (full text).</ref>
